items.brief: Search intent 2.1 to 5.5, up 161.9% in a day, while search interest went the other way and slipped 1.1%. That combination usually means people are looking for something specific rather than browsing, and here the site says what: Groove.cm is becoming Scale.gg, new enrollment is closed, and existing members keep access. The spike is people finding out it is shutting to newcomers, not demand arriving. Worth recording precisely because the score reads it as a rise and the page says otherwise.

The stack is the odd detail, carrying twelve separate payment processors, which is far more than a shop this size needs unless it is selling into several countries with local methods in each.

Existing members keep their access, and the site carries eleven separate payment processors from the years it was selling hard.

combined.name: hnglance.com
combined.brief: A pricing page appeared where there was none, with three tiers on it, and the traffic rank improved 2.1% in the same day. The pricing signal is the one that matters: it is the moment somebody decides a side project is a product. The Hacker News numbers behind it are four points and four comments, so almost nobody has noticed yet, and that is the interesting part rather than a reason to discount it.
combined.description: A reader that shows the current Hacker News front page as a single view of what the site is talking about, rather than a ranked list you scroll. It has just started charging, with three tiers where there was previously nothing to buy.

combined.name: luma-touch.com
combined.brief: Second day. Japan 50 to 41 and the best position with it, but the United States went 63 to 64 and the number of countries charting fell from three to two. Yesterday's move was three storefronts climbing together; today only one is still climbing. That is what the end of a promotion looks like, and the next two days decide whether the Japanese gain was the same wave arriving late or something holding on its own.
combined.description: LumaFusion is a professional multi-track video and audio editor for iPad, iPhone and Android, made by Luma Touch. It is sold as a paid app with optional add-ons rather than a subscription, and is aimed at mobile journalists, filmmakers and social video producers who edit on a tablet instead of a desktop.

combined.name: kaylees.site
combined.brief: Second day running. Britain 44 to 26 and the best position 18 to 16, after yesterday's move from 40 to 18 across three storefronts. The first day could have been a feature slot; a second day of gains in the same direction is harder to explain that way, and the app is still paid, so the buying has continued rather than a promotion having ended.
combined.description: The site of an independent developer selling paid iPhone apps, whose entire statement of intent is that they make apps for humans. The apps are bought outright rather than subscribed to, which is why they appear on the paid charts rather than the free ones.

combined.name: arredocasadasogno.com
combined.brief: Traffic rank 102,193 to 89,988, a climb of 12,205 places in a day, alongside a fourth pricing tier appearing where there were three. Three unrelated collectors saw it: one measuring traffic, one reading the pricing page, one reading the technology stack. The stack is the odd detail, carrying twelve separate payment processors, which is far more than a shop this size needs unless it is selling into several countries with local methods in each.
combined.description: An Italian online shop selling homeware, textiles and furnishing accessories. It carries twelve separate payment processors, which is a lot for a shop this size and usually means it sells across several countries with local methods in each.

combined.name: simplecommenter.com
combined.brief: Downloads 2,425 to 2,649, so 224 installations in a day against 200 sites actively running it, and ratings 12 to 13. Small numbers, and worth saying so plainly: this is a young plugin and a fifth of everyone who has ever downloaded it did so today. What makes it worth a second look rather than a dismissal is that the download count and the traffic rank moved together, which two unrelated collectors had to agree on.
combined.description: A commenting tool that sits on top of a live website so a client can point at what they want changed. It replaces the email thread of screenshots and vague descriptions that agency review normally runs on, and charges for it on two tiers.

combined.name: storyreel.life
combined.brief: Three independent sources saw this and they disagree, which is the interesting part. Its pricing page went from two tiers to three while its US chart position slipped 45 to 47 and the number of countries it charts in halved from two to one. Adding a paid tier as attention narrows is a monetisation decision, not growth, and 31,066 ratings say the audience it has is already large enough to charge.
combined.description: A short drama app, serving the vertical video serials that have grown into their own category: episodes of a minute or two, shot for a phone held upright, released in runs of fifty or more. The format is watched in a queue rather than sat down in front of, and the apps carrying it monetise by charging to unlock the next episode.

combined.name: ottokit.com
combined.brief: Downloads 3,152,066 to 3,176,891 in a day, which is 24,825 installations of a WordPress plugin in twenty four hours, against 90,000 sites running it. Traffic rank improved 2.0% over the same window, so two unrelated collectors moved together: one counting installs and one counting visits. The plugin also went from nine pricing tiers to ten, which is a company adjusting what it charges rather than what it ships.
combined.description: A no code automation platform for WordPress, wiring the plugins a site already runs and the outside services it depends on into workflows without any glue code in between. It was called SureTriggers until the rename, and it sells against Zapier by living inside the site rather than calling it from outside.
